neighbours.label: Contrasting then with now: how things were in the past set against today
fire: Decent wetsuits weren't around when surfing first caught on.
Life was much harder back then, but children today have it easy.
Polio would be as frightening today as it was in 1950.
Shopping was so much slower in those days.
Teachers used to hit pupils, but they would never do that today.
People today complain about flights. But spare a thought for sailors in 1700.
Phones were a luxury in my childhood, unlike now.
Mail took weeks when my grandparents were young.
quiet: Decent wetsuits aren't cheap when you buy them in town.
Life is much harder in winter, but children here have warm coats.
Polio can be frightening for parents with no vaccine.
Shopping is so much slower at the weekend.
Teachers often help pupils, and they will do that tomorrow.
People often complain about flights. They also complain about trains.
Phones are a problem in my classroom, like tablets.
Mail takes days when the roads are closed.

predictions: Past-against-present wording fires; present-tense statements in the same frame stay quiet.
